description: Iron is a chemical element with symbol Fe and atomic number 26. It is a metal belonging to the first transition series and group 8 of the periodic table, and is by mass the most common element on Earth, forming much of Earth's outer and inner core.
uses: Iron alloys such as steel, stainless steel, cast iron and special steels are the most common industrial metals due to their mechanical properties and low cost. Iron is also essential to human biology, being a key component of hemoglobin and myoglobin proteins that transport and store oxygen. Additionally, iron is the active site metal in many important redox enzymes involved in cellular respiration and oxidation-reduction processes in plants and animals.
characteristics: Pristine pure iron surfaces are mirror-like silvery-gray, but iron readily reacts with oxygen and water to produce brown-to-black hydrated iron oxides known as rust. Below its Curie point of 770°C, iron is ferromagnetic with unpaired electrons that align to create an overall magnetic field. Iron has four stable isotopes and forms compounds in oxidation states ranging from −2 to +7, also forming many coordination complexes with industrial, medical, or research applications.
